newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan won't raise taxes further for now -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan won't raise taxes further for now -- MOF.

text.p: The Japanese government will not raise taxes for the time being, apart from a scheduled increase in the consumption tax on April 1, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said on Wednesday.
Asked whether the government would carry out its plan for fiscal reform without raising taxes until the year 2003, Mitsuzuka said: "For the time being, we will not raise taxes."
He did not elaborate further on the period.

On Tuesday, the government announced it would speed up fical reform, aiming to reduce the state deficit to three percent or less of annual gross domestic product by 2003, shortening the period from the original target of 2005.
The government also pledged to stop issues of deficit-financing bonds by 2003, instead of 2005.
Mitsuzuka also said the government will cut its fiscal loan and investment programme in the fiscal year starting in April 1998.
"It was a minus for the 1997/98 year and we will stick to that pace for the 1998/99 year," he said.

The programme, which collects funds from public pension and postal savings and makes loans to quasi-governmental financial institutions, will be 39.33 trillion yen in 1997/98, down 3.0 percent from this year.
